params.body:
The server side of the Studio's new writing view: the conversation writes in the piece instead of in the chat.

## What changes

**Suggestions as tracked changes.** When the Studio sends `piece: true` with a chat message, an answer may end in `<suggestion>` blocks. They never reach the chat text; each is stored in a new `article_suggestions` table as a tracked change on one paragraph (or one slide) with the sources it rests on. Every source id the model names is checked against the Observatory's tables and dropped when it is not a row there. On accept, each source is cited under its sentence through `article_evidence.anchor`, so the body stays plain markdown and the site renders exactly what it rendered before.

- `GET /articles/:id/suggestions`, `POST /articles/:id/suggestions/:sid/accept` (`{version, body, text}`: accepts against unsaved text, and typed-over text becomes the writer's own with its anchors moved to the nearest sentence) and `.../dismiss`. Author or admin only, behind the existing visibility guard.
- A newer answer replaces what is pending at the same place; a replacement whose paragraph the writer has since changed is refused with a 409 instead of overwriting it.
- `POST /articles/:id/review/preview {body}` runs ProveML's existing review summary against unsaved text, so the Studio shows "x of y citations checked, n numbers without a source" while the writer types. Nothing is stored; nothing new is built in ProveML.
- `GET /articles/:id` adds a `card` per evidence row in the Studio route only (what, source, region, date, cohorts). The site's projection is untouched.

**Choices as buttons.** An answer that asks the writer to pick (an angle, go ahead or not) ends with a `<choices>` block of two to four short replies, sent to the Studio as buttons and kept with the message.

**Three shapes of a piece.** `articles.format` (post, article, deck) and `articles.deck_brand` (gentells, trendwolves). Only a post goes to gentells.com: choosing an article or a deck makes the piece own work, and pointing it at the site makes it a post again. A deck's blocks are slides separated by `---`. On an empty piece the chat sets the shape, title and standfirst it read from the conversation, with a deterministic backstop when the model does not name the shape (slides asked for in the writer's words and every block written as a slide).

**The prompt** (`packages/pipeline/piece-prompt.mjs`) carries the six ways a writer arrives (a thesis gets evidence for and against first), options only when asked, asking before bigger steps, never inventing scenes or numbers a source does not carry, and a short reminder of both blocks right before the answer, where the model reliably reads it.

**Model.** Sonnet 5.5 (`claude-sonnet-5-5`, $2/$10, same as Sonnet 5) joins the catalog and becomes the default for `content-chat`, still headless through the Claude CLI. Measured side by side on the same requests against a local copy of the Studio: 7 to 18 s per answer against 10 to 38 s for Haiku 4.5, sources attached when it wrote, buttons every time, and no details beyond what the signals say, where Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5 both added some. The pipeline's own Sonnet phases stay on Sonnet 5. A `content-chat` model saved in Settings still wins over this default.

## Safe to merge alone

The new behaviour only runs when the Studio asks for it (`piece: true`); the Studio build now on the box keeps the chat it was built against. The new tables and columns are additive (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN` in `try`). The Studio's matching change is a separate pull request and may land before or after this one.

## Tests

`node --test test/*.test.mjs`: 1074 of 1080 pass on a fresh worktree from main. The six that fail are `report-render`, which needs `pdftoppm`, not installed on the machine that ran them; they fail the same on main there. New: `test/suggestions.test.mjs` (parsing, source checks, anchoring, accept and dismiss, formats and slides, choices, the routes) and a catalog test that pins the chat to Sonnet 5.5 on the CLI.

Tried end to end against a local server and a seeded database: a thesis, a hunch, an opening paragraph, and two pitch decks drafted by the chat, accepted, and exported.
params.title: Studio chat writes in the piece: suggestions with checked sources, post/article/deck, Sonnet 5.5
